findings.reason: Confirmed. Item almost-category is stated for 'an almost base (V,m) with m²=m and the required flatness of m⊗_V m', and its API AlmostElements.hom asserts '(N^a)_*=Hom_V(m,N)'. In that generality the right adjoint is Hom_V(m̃, N) with m̃ = m⊗_V m (Gabber–Ramero, (2.2.4) and Proposition 2.2.13). The two agree only when multiplication m̃ → m is an isomorphism, for instance when m is flat. I checked the counterexample. Let V be the valuation ring of the completion of F_p((t^{1/p^∞})), m its maximal ideal, W = V/(t) and n = mW = m/tV. Then n² = n, and by right exactness n ⊗_W n = (m⊗_V m)/(t·m) ≅ m/tm (since m is V-flat with m⊗m ≅ m² = m), which is W-flat as a base change of m. The multiplication m/tm → m/tV has kernel tV/tm ≅ V/m ≠ 0. So (W, n) satisfies the item's hypotheses, but the identity of ñ does not factor through ñ → n, and Hom_W(n, ñ) ≠ Hom_W(ñ, ñ). The fix is right: state the general API with Hom_V(m̃, N), and derive Hom_V(m, N) when m is flat (the perfectoid valuation case Bhatt uses, footnote 5). It is an extraction error, not a source erratum.
